chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who performed an Umrah al-Mufrada, then had intercourse with his wife before completing his Tawaf and Sa'i. He said: 'Upon him is a camel (as expiation) for the invalidity of his Umrah, and he must remain until the following month, then go to one of the Miqat places and enter into Ihram with an Umrah.'
And the ruling for one who masturbated until he ejaculated is the same as the ruling for one who had intercourse in the same manner; he narred that.

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A specific type of camel used as expiation (kaffarah)
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Umrah performed independently, without combining it with Hajj
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتٌ: Designated places where pilgrims enter the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who has intercourse before completing Umrah rituals?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that premature sexual intercourse invalidates the Umrah al-Mufrada, requiring the pilgrim to offer a camel (Badana) as expiation and perform a new Umrah after waiting for the next lunar month. The narration further establishes the legal equivalence between masturbation and sexual intercourse regarding the penalty, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the nullification of the state of Ihram. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining ritual purity and the specific conditions of the pilgrimage rites as interpreted by the Ahl al-Bayt.
